dossier_meta.authors: Albertson, Michael O., Grossman, Sara, Haas, Ruth
dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory » Coloring » Vertex coloring
dossier_meta.statement_text: Conjecture Let $ G $ be a simple graph with $ n $ vertices and list chromatic number $ \chi_\ell(G) $ . Suppose that $ 0\leq t\leq \chi_\ell $ and each vertex of $ G $ is assigned a list of $ t $ colors. Then at least $ \frac{tn}{\chi_\ell(G)} $ vertices of $ G $ can be colored from these lists.
dossier_meta.context_text: Albertson, Grossman, and Haas introduce this interesting question in [AGH], and prove some partial results. For instance, they show that under the above assumptions, at least $ (1 - (\frac{ \chi(G) - 1}{\chi(G)} )^t) \cdot n $ vertices of $ G $ can be colored from the lists.
dossier_meta.references_text: - *[AGH] M. Albertson, S. Grossman and R. Haas, Partial list colouring, Discrete Math., 214(2000), pp. 235-240.
